answer: Each identity claims one jetty pile in karst bedrock and locks an 80-credit bond, one pile per key, marked by an umber band. Each epoch it files the band's exposed length. An auditor recomputes scour from the karst table using diameter and current speed, burning the bond for an error over 5 percent, a reused band, or a duplicate pile. The first costs 39 credits, the kth 39+7(k-1), so 1,000 fakes cost 3,535,500 plus 80,000 locked bonds. A rented-pile farm fails because one pile yields only one scour reading. An honest claimant pays 39 once and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
